decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation/spec required manual title entry; Round 1 client: “I'd have to type in a title myself every time... I really just want to paste the web address.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client replaced the title-required save flow with reference-conforming URL-only saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation omitted automatic metadata capture; Round 1 client requested that the app “fill in the page's title (and its little site icon) ... automatically.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client surfaced and requested part of the missing automatic-metadata requirement. Description and preview-image capture were not requested.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export... excluded from the first release”; Round 1 client: “I'm fine leaving out... import/export... for now.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identified and accepted omission of Netscape HTML import.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export... excluded from the first release”; Round 1 client: “I'm fine leaving out... import/export... for now.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identified and accepted omission of Netscape HTML export.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “tags”; Round 1 client said tags “sound right,” and Round 5 client later reported “I added... tags.”
decisions.note: The presented and implemented tag-assignment behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “sorting”; Round 5 client later verified that “sorting by title” returned the expected result.
decisions.note: Sorting by a selectable key is reference-conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “URL-only bookmark saving”; Round 2 client: “I can just paste a link,” and approved the revision.
decisions.note: The revised specification directly conforms to URL-only saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed automatic “page-title and site-icon capture,” but no description or preview-image capture; Round 2 client called the title/icon behavior “exactly what I was hoping for” without mentioning the omitted fields.
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, metadata capture remained narrower than REF-BM-02. The approval did not surface the missing description and preview image.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker offered “Editable captured titles”; Round 2 client approved being able to “tweak the title,” without requesting description editing or editing both before and after save.
decisions.note: The revised specification exposed only captured-title editing, short of editable title and description before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker selected “transactional substring search”; Round 3 client reiterated only generic “search” and approved the plan.
decisions.note: At the planning gate, literal substring search omits the reference query language: #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, and quoted exact phrases.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker described “substring search” but did not state which bookmark fields are searched or whether matching is case-insensitive; Round 3 client only said the app should “let me search.”
decisions.note: The planning record cannot establish conformity or divergence for required field coverage and case-insensitive matching.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker placed “URL-only saving” in the MVP; Round 4 client approved “saving a link with just the address.”
decisions.note: The task-breakdown decision conforms to URL-only saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker scoped the MVP to “automatic title/icon capture”; Round 4 client approved that same scope without raising description or preview-image capture.
decisions.note: At the task-breakdown gate, the planned metadata fields were still incomplete relative to REF-BM-02.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker listed “title editing” in the MVP; Round 4 client approved “editable titles” without raising description editing or pre-save editing.
decisions.note: At the task-breakdown gate, the editing decision remained narrower than REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presented “duplicate handling”; its implementation disposition appears in Round 5, where the client reports that a repeat save “warned me it was already there and pointed me to the existing one.”
decisions.note: Linked task and implementation evidence shows the duplicate flow guides the user to the existing bookmark rather than silently creating another.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker included “reopening links” in the MVP; Round 4 client explicitly approved that capability.
decisions.note: Reopening a saved link is functionally consistent with navigation to its original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered “URL-only saving”; Round 5 client tested “Saving with just a link” and reported that it worked.
decisions.note: The implementation-stage decision conforms to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker's completed feature list still names only “automatic title/icon capture”; the client reviewed title/icon behavior but did not mention description or preview-image capture.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the delivered metadata scope remained incomplete, and the missing description/preview fields passed without expression.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claimed automatic title/icon capture was delivered; Round 5 client: “the automatic title/icon pull didn't complete... it fell back every time,” but called this “not a blocker” and accepted the app.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client explicitly surfaced the difference between promised capture and observed all-fallback behavior, then accepted it based on the fallback and trust that reachable pages would work.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker declared implementation complete with generic “Search”; the implemented design followed Round 3's substring-search decision. Round 5 client tested ordinary search but did not raise #tag syntax, Boolean grouping, or quoted phrases.
decisions.note: The implementation review supplied another opportunity to surface the planned restricted search language, but the response did not do so.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker listed “Search”; Round 5 client said search returned expected results, but neither identified the indexed fields or case behavior.
decisions.note: Implementation-review evidence is insufficient to determine full-text field coverage or case-insensitive matching.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered tags; Round 5 client verified “I added... tags.”
decisions.note: The implemented assignment of tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered tags and the client added them, but neither presentation nor response states whether existing tags are offered as autocomplete.
decisions.note: The tag-entry decision is recorded, but autocomplete behavior cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered tags; Round 5 client verified “filtering by... tag” returned the expected bookmarks.
decisions.note: Filtering to a selected tag's bookmarks conforms to REF-BM-11.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered sorting; Round 5 client verified “sorting by title” behaved as expected.
decisions.note: The implementation-stage sorting behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claimed “Full editing”; Round 5 client verified edits to title, notes, folder, and tags, but the record does not establish editing of URL or description.
decisions.note: The implementation review does not contain enough evidence to classify the complete required edit-field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivered “confirmed deletion”; Round 5 client reported that deletion was confirmed and “actually removed the item everywhere.”
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion is implemented; confirmation is an additional compatible safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client reported “I added notes,” but neither maker nor client states that notes accept Markdown and render it when viewed.
decisions.note: Generic note support is established, but Markdown authoring/rendering cannot be classified.
